question: Arundhati Roy won the Booker Prize for which novel?
solution:
The correct answer is __**The God of Small Things**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• **Arundhati Roy** was awarded the prestigious **Booker Prize** in **1997** for her debut novel, **The God of Small Things**. This achievement made her the first **Indian citizen** residing in India to win this world-renowned literary award. *Hence, option 1 is correct.*

• **Midnight's Children** is a celebrated novel by **Salman Rushdie**, which won the **Booker Prize** in **1981**. It later received the **Booker of Bookers** in **1993** and the **Best of the Booker** in **2008**. *Hence, option 2 is incorrect.*

• **The White Tiger** was authored by **Aravind Adiga** and won the **Man Booker Prize** in **2008**. The novel provides a dark and humorous perspective on the class struggle in **India** through the protagonist **Balram Halwai**. *Hence, option 3 is incorrect.*

• **The Guide** is one of the most famous works by **R.K. Narayan**, published in **1958**. While it won the **Sahitya Akademi Award** in **1960** and was adapted into a famous **Bollywood** film, it did not win the Booker Prize. *Hence, option 4 is incorrect.*

**Additional Information__**

__

• **Arundhati Roy** was born on **November 24, 1961**, in **Shillong**, **Meghalaya**. She is not only a novelist but also a prominent **political activist** known for her advocacy on **human rights** and **environmental issues**.

• **The God of Small Things** is set in **Aymanam**, **Kerala**, and explores the childhood experiences of fraternal twins **Estha** and **Rahel**. It delves into complex themes such as the **Caste System**, **Communism**, and the **Love Laws** that govern social interactions in **India**.

• The **Booker Prize** (formerly the **Man Booker Prize**) was established in **1969**. It is awarded annually to the best sustained work of fiction written in the **English language** and published in the **United Kingdom** or **Ireland**.

• Other notable **Indian-origin** winners of the Booker Prize include **V.S. Naipaul** for **In a Free State** (**1971**) and **Kiran Desai** for **The Inheritance of Loss** (**2006**).

• In **2022**, **Geetanjali Shree** became the first **Indian author** to win the **International Booker Prize** for her novel **Ret Samadhi**, translated into English as **Tomb of Sand**.

**Important Points__**

• **The God of Small Things** was a massive international success, being translated into more than **40 languages** and selling millions of copies worldwide.

• Following her literary debut, **Arundhati Roy** turned her focus toward **non-fiction** and **essays**, publishing works like **The Algebra of Infinite Justice**, **Listening to Grasshoppers**, and **Broken Republic**.

• Her second novel, **The Ministry of Utmost Happiness**, was published in **2017**, exactly **20 years** after her first novel, and was longlisted for the **Man Booker Prize** that same year.

• Roy has been a vocal critic of **globalization**, **nuclear weapons**, and the **Narmada Dam project**, often using her platform to highlight the struggles of marginalized communities in **India**.
